## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
`Cache.set` needs fixing before merge. It stores keys without lower-casing them, but `get` always looks up the lower-cased key. Any mixed-case key written through `set` is unreadable and is never evicted. The added round-trip test uses a key that is already lowercase, so it passes despite the bug. Both changed files were read in full; the `DEFAULT_TTL` change and its updated comment are consistent with each other and with the new test.

## Critical
- app/cache.py:27 — correctness — `c.set("Alpha", 1)` followed by `c.get("Alpha")` (or `c.get("alpha")`) returns `None`, because `set` writes `self._store[key]` with the raw key while `get` reads `self._store.get(key.lower())` (app/cache.py:17). This breaks the invariant documented at app/cache.py:14-15: "every path into _store lower-cases the key first, or mixed-case callers create duplicate entries that never expire together". `test_set_then_get_round_trip` (tests/test_cache.py:10-14) only calls `set("alpha", 1)`, so it cannot catch this. The fix is to write `self._store[key.lower()] = (value, time.monotonic() + self._ttl)` and change the test to set a mixed-case key such as `"Alpha"` and read it back as both `"alpha"` and `"ALPHA"`. — Callers using mixed-case keys always miss the cache with no error. Those entries also stay in `_store` forever, because the delete-on-expiry path in `get` only removes lower-cased keys, so memory grows without bound.

## Strengths
- `test_entries_expire` (tests/test_cache.py:21-27) checks expiry against a monkeypatched `time.monotonic`. The test is deterministic and does not need to sleep, and the patch takes effect because `app/cache.py` calls `time.monotonic` through the module.
- The `DEFAULT_TTL` comment at app/cache.py:7 was updated together with the value, and `test_default_ttl_is_five_minutes` pins the new value.
